processing: Organic and biodynamically farmed leaf, handled in the usual Darjeeling way for black tea: withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, lighter in spring.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, first flush in spring, second flush in early summer and an autumn picking.
appearance_dry: Typical of whole-leaf Darjeeling: wiry leaf, greener in spring and browner in summer.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in spring, amber to copper in later flushes.
appearance_wet: Mixed green and copper leaf, darker in later flushes.
taste_profile: Varies by lot. As with Darjeeling generally, spring brings florals and briskness, summer rounder fruit and autumn a mellow woodiness.

brewing.notes: Western style. Cooler and shorter for spring lots; hotter water for summer and autumn.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and harvest year, with the organic status as a main selling point. Drink spring lots within about a year. Since family ownership ended in 2014, judge recent lots on their own merit.
description:
Makaibari, in the Kurseong valley, is the Darjeeling garden most tied to organic farming. It became India's first certified organic tea estate in 1988 and the first with biodynamic certification in 1993.

Those certifications are about the land more than the factory. In Darjeeling they also helped with erosion, unstable slopes and worn-out soil, problems that heavy chemical use had made worse. The leaf itself is processed in the regional manner.

Brew it as you would any Darjeeling, adjusting for the flush. Taste depends on the lot, so spring and autumn teas from this garden can be quite unlike each other.

Buy by flush and year, and look for current certification on the label instead of relying on the garden's older reputation. Tasting one spring and one summer lot side by side is a good next step.
history:
Accounts of the start differ. One says Captain Samler, an agent of the Darjeeling Tea Company, founded it in 1852 and sold to Girish Chandra Banerjee; others credit Banerjee with founding it in 1859. A factory was commissioned there in 1859 and closed in 1933. It is described as Darjeeling's first, while the estate's own claim of the world's first has no independent backing.

The garden passed through the Banerjee family to Swaraj Kumar 'Rajah' Banerjee, the last family owner. He sold a majority stake to the Kolkata-based Luxmi Group in 2014 and left in 2017, handing over to Rudra Chatterjee.
